research.title: New Mexico Film Permits: 3 Important Permitting Facts - PPS
research.excerpt: #### Requirements # New Mexico Film Permits [Request Permit Consultation](https://grouppps.com/film-permit-quote/) ## **New Mexico Film Permit Requirements** **What are the permit requirements to film in New Mexico\*\*** Filming in New Mexico requires securing the appropriate New Mexico film permits to ensure that production activities comply with state and local laws. These permits are typically required for filming on public property, streets, or any other public spaces, and they help to regulate access to filming locations. Filmmakers must provide detailed information about the project, including location, dates, times, and the nature of the filming activities. It’s essential to apply for New Mexico film permits in advance to avoid any last-minute complications and to ensure that all necessary permits are in place before production begins. ... Filmmakers must work closely with local authorities to meet these requirements and avoid fines or delays. The permit process also ensures that filmmakers maintain the safety of their crew, cast, and the public during filming, which is crucial when filming in public spaces or urban environments. Filmmakers should also be prepared for additional permitting requirements if they plan to film in certain special locations in New Mexico, such as national parks, monuments, or other protected areas. These areas often have strict environmental regulations, and additional New Mexico film permits may be required to film in these locations. Productions that impact the environment or use natural features for their scenes must ensure they meet all the required criteria to protect New Mexico’s natural resources. Permits for these areas are typically more detailed and require advanced planning to ensure compliance.

research.excerpt: The deep vendor network and experienced crew base mean that most department-head positions can be filled locally, reducing travel costs. ## New Mexico film incentive, _at a glance._ The questions producers ask first when sizing a New Mexicoshoot, answered against the state's current program structure and fringe environment. Is the New Mexico film tax credit refundable or transferable? New Mexico's film tax credit is refundable, meaning the state pays out the credit as cash regardless of the production company's in-state tax liability. Payouts typically arrive 6 to 18 months after a final certified audit. What is the New Mexico film incentive rate? New Mexico's base rate is 25% on qualified production spend, with stackable uplifts that can push the effective top rate to 40% (+10% rural (60+ mi from ABQ/Santa Fe); +5% TV pilot/series; +5% qualified facility). What is the minimum spend to qualify for the New Mexico film incentive? The minimum qualified-spend threshold to access the New Mexico program is None. Productions below this threshold are not eligible for the incentive. What is the annual cap on the New Mexico film tax credit? New Mexico's annual program cap is $140M (FY2026). Productions should confirm current fund availability before committing, as caps can be exhausted mid-fiscal-year. What is the payroll burden for film production in New Mexico? Typical payroll burden in New Mexico runs 24–28% on top of gross wages, covering payroll taxes, statutory insurance, and applicable union pension/health/welfare contributions. Workers' compensation rates for production work generally fall around 3.99%, and production purchases are subject to 5.125% GRT. research.excerpt: # Permit Information Although comparatively few permits are necessary for filming in New Mexico, permits are required for production on federal, state-owned, and tribal properties and lands. Permits are also often required for production on city properties, especially historical sites, and public streets, as well as for special use of county roads and state highways. **\*** Companies considering shooting on federal property must connect with the proper federal contact. * * * ### Location Permits * The New Mexico Film Office does not issue filming permits. * Film permitting is generally handled by the city/town/county where you're filming. For permit questions specific to a location, please get in touch with the nearest film liaison. * State-owned properties: Please contact the NMFO at 505-476-5600 or via email at info@nmfilm.com * * * ### Railroad Right of Entry and Permitting Please get in touch with the [NMDOT Rail Bureau | NMDOT](https://www.dot.nm. gov/planning-research-multimodal-and-safety/modal/transit-rail/rail-bureau/) via email with any inquiries or questions about potential encroachment on railroad property. If you are within 100 feet of a railroad or between a fence/property marker and a railroad, you may be trespassing in the railroad right-of-way and can conflict with railroad operations which can create a serious safety hazard for the railroad and film production. This includes production at NM Rail Runner Express stations and Amtrak Stations. Filming activities may be interrupted if you fail to obtain written permission from the railroad owner to enter its property. In New Mexico, the three most prominent railroad property owners are BNSF Railway, Union Pacific Railroad, and the New Mexico Department of Transportation (NMDOT). research.excerpt: Film Las Cruces is contracted with the City of Las Cruces, Doña Ana County and the City of Anthony to provide permitting assistance to film and digital media projects. We are happy to walk you through and point you in the right direction for all other permitting agencies throughout southern New Mexico; including White Sands National Park, Town of Mesilla, Bureau of Land Management, Spaceport America, Hatch, New Mexico Department of Transportation, and others. ##### What kinds of filming activities do not require a permit? News and gathering of news related stories. Other types of documentaries not requiring the use of actors, models, sets, or props. Still not sure if your production requires a filming permit? Give us a call: 575-805-3456 ##### What is a low impact/b-roll permit? A low impact/b-roll filming permit may be issued for documentary-style footage with a maximum of 8 total cast and crew on-site at any one time. ##### When should I notify neighboring residents and businesses regarding filming activity in the area? All permitted filming locations are likely to require the surrounding businesses and neighbors to be notified of your filming activity 48 hours in advance of load in. The standard radius for notification letter distribution is 200 feet from the filming location, parking, and basecamp.
